content.title: About
content.content: Kernza flour is made from the grains of the hybrid pseudo‑cereal Kernza (Thinopyrum intermedium). The pre‑gelatinized version has undergone partial starch hydrolysis, improving its solubility in cold liquids and accelerating dough viscosity. The flour has a light nutty aroma, a pale brown color, and is suitable for gluten‑free recipes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Kernza is one of the first commercially cultivated pseudo‑cereals designed for climate‑resilient agriculture.
The grain contains over 50 % complex carbohydrates and a high level of dietary fiber.
Pre‑gelatinized flour swells quickly in cold water, making it convenient for sauces and smoothies.
Kernza requires less water and fertilizer than wheat, reducing its environmental footprint.
The flour retains most of the protein and minerals of the original grain.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: A high mix of soluble and insoluble fibers supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Partially gelatinized starch is digested slowly, helping to stabilize blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: The flour provides about 12 % plant‑based protein, beneficial for vegetarians and vegans.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: It supplies magnesium, phosphorus, iron, and zinc, important for bone and metabolic health.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Phenolic compounds in Kernza help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Pseudo‑cereal allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to Kernza proteins.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or fermentation is advisable for heavy consumers.

items.title: High fiber load
items.content: Large amounts may cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use Kernza flour in gluten‑free breads, pancakes, muffins, and to thicken sauces, soups, or smoothies. Its pre‑gelatinized nature allows it to dissolve in cold liquids without lengthy soaking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.
